title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 69
paragraphs: When she spoke this way to Mardonius, those friendly to Artemisia were distressed by her words, supposing she would suffer some harm from the king for urging him not to fight at sea, while those who envied and resented her — because she had been honored above all the allies — rejoiced at the contradiction, supposing she was now ruined. When, however, the various opinions were reported to Xerxes, he was greatly pleased with Artemisia's; and whereas he had already thought her excellent, he commended her now even more. Nevertheless he gave orders to follow the advice of the majority, believing that when they had fought at Euboea they had been deliberately slack because he was not present, whereas now he had made himself ready to watch while they fought the battle.
